items.title: PolinRider Malware Force-Pushed Into AsyncAPI, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts Pull Requests
items.description: PolinRider malware was force-pushed into AsyncAPI, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts pull requests and ran in CircuitVerse's release CI. How it works, IOCs, and how to check your projects.

items.title: Fail2Install (CVE-2026-132165): Drupal Installer Flaw Lets Attackers Take Over Sites and Run Code
items.description: Drupal CVE-2026-132165 (Fail2Install) is an unauthenticated installer flaw that can reinstall a live site and run code. We reproduced the re-entry, confirmed the fix, and show how to detect and block it.

items.title: The Take-Home Test That Runs on Your Work Laptop: Inside the AccuraSoftHire Fake Interview Campaign
items.description: Binance says its $6.34 billion theft began when an engineer ran a fake interview assignment on his work computer. JFrog has now exposed a fake company, AccuraSoftHire, built to run the same trick. We decoded the attacker's server history from a public Ethereum wallet and found npm packages from the interview task that stayed installable for up to seven months. Here is what to check on your developer machines.

items.title: nginx2root (CVE-2026-123007): HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code on Unpatched nginx Servers
items.description: nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 fix an HTTP/2 flaw that a public exploit turns into unauthenticated code execution. See what stopped the exploit in our lab, how to patch and confirm the fix, and how to find nginx on developer machines.

items.title: Protecting where software gets built: StepSecurity’s $20 million Series A
items.description: Today, we’re announcing an oversubscribed $20 million Series A led by Elephant to expand protection for developer machines, package downloads, CI/CD pipelines, and agent sandboxes.

items.title: OPTIMJACK: Optimizely-Hosted Scripts Loaded a Crypto Clipper and Card Skimmer on 178 Organizations
items.description: Optimizely confirmed an attacker injected malicious JavaScript into customer projects. What the payload does, who was hit, and what to check.

items.title: Introducing the StepSecurity Secure Registry Community Tier, Integrated with Harden-Runner
items.description: Today, we’re making the StepSecurity Secure Registry available for free as part of our community tier, and integrating it with Harden-Runner to make it easier to adopt in GitHub Actions.

items.title: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI Package Compromised
items.description: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package, published November 17, contain Python startup hooks that harvest cloud and CI/CD credentials and attempt to obtain identity tokens. Both releases send collected data to a webhook.site endpoint. PyPI quarantined both versions; the second malicious release was uploaded after the first quarantine.

items.title: Harden-Runner Brings Runtime Security Inside Kata and Nitro Runner Pods
items.description: Harden-Runner monitors GitHub Actions jobs and enforces egress policies inside runner microVMs on Kata Containers and Amazon EKS Nitro Sandboxes.

items.title: New StepSecurity Control: Audit GitHub Fork PR Workflow Approval Policies
items.description: StepSecurity’s new control flags GitHub organizations and public repositories that let fork pull request workflows run without approval.

items.title: WPPConnect Compromised: Malicious Releases Steal Secrets and WhatsApp Sessions Through the Project's Own Pipeline
items.description: Malicious WPPConnect npm releases 2.4.1 and 2.10.82 steal secrets and WhatsApp sessions via Telegram. Affected versions, how they shipped and what to rotate.

items.title: ARTEX: Attackers Adopted This AI Pentesting Tool in Three Months. Leaked Secrets Are Its Fastest Way In.
items.description: ARTEX is an open-source tool where AI agents run a penetration test on their own. Since August 2026, state-aligned groups, criminal crews and one runaway research agent have pointed ARTEX at hundreds of organizations. In one case, an agent went from a GitHub search for leaked secrets to stolen cloud data in five minutes. This post covers what ARTEX is, who uses ARTEX, how to spot ARTEX activity, and how you remove its easiest way in.

items.title: CVE-2026-126187: React Server Components Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Code Through Smuggled Flight Rows
items.description: React shipped fixes on November 10, 2026 for a CVSS 9.5 unauthenticated RCE in React Server Components' Flight protocol. Read how a silent serialization bug turns typed arrays into code execution, who is exposed, and how to find affected installs in CI and on developer machines.

items.title: WFX Phantom: The GitHub Actions Secret Stealer That Deletes Its Tracks
items.description: A coordinated botnet of compromised GitHub accounts launched a widespread attack, opening seemingly harmless pull requests before pushing a malicious shell script directly to default branches. The script, dubbed "wfx", executed through GitHub Actions to steal secrets before the attackers quickly reverted their changes, leaving minimal traces.

items.title: GitHub Package Firewall vs. StepSecurity Secure Registry: Protection beyond npm
items.description: GitHub’s package firewall covers npm only. StepSecurity's Secure Registry protects 8 ecosystems, traces every install, and blocks malicious packages within an hour

items.title: Railway’s Security Incident: Why CI/CD Needs Runtime Security
items.description: Lessons from Railway’s November 10 report: review build access, tighten OIDC trust, and use Harden-Runner to observe and restrict CI/CD runtime activity.

items.title: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 Compromised
items.description: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 is compromised. Malicious install-time code targets Swarm wallet data and attempts to establish persistent access on affected systems.

items.title: CVE-2026-123158 (*sshole): OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on Alpine Linux
items.description: CVE-2026-123158 (*sshole) enables an OpenSSH authentication bypass on Alpine Linux. Review lab results, exposure conditions, fixes, and mitigations.

items.title: CVE-2026-109518: apt Flaw Lets Attackers Swap Packages After Verification and Run Code as Root
items.description: Understand CVE-2026-109518, patch vulnerable APT clients, and use Harden-Runner to find HTTP package downloads and investigate CI/CD activity.

items.title: Malicious Files: Find What Supply Chain Attacks Leave Behind in Your GitHub Repositories and on Developer Machines
items.description: StepSecurity Malicious Files finds files planted by Miasma, Shai-Hulud and other supply chain attacks in GitHub repositories and on developer machines.
